layout.why: the brief and page 11 decision 9: the set stands on the world's axes and is seen at the engine's angle; nothing is built square to the camera. The old path already climbed on a slant from the bottom left: its marks 0 to 4 lie on one -y line within 1 px, so the path runs along -y there; its first leg, through the arch, runs along +x, so that whoever leaves goes through the arch and on up the path off the picture's edge (sevan). The arch could not stand across the path's climb: the old picture's lower left holds Carmen, Luis, abuela, the frog and the dog at the end of story 14, and a post there would stand in front of one of them. The three small trees keep their old feet (the birds, the cat in them, Carmen's places by them are all relative to them): free-standing round trees, not a row (a row along -y through the middle one, trees=row in the set's address, puts the first tree's trunk behind the arch and the third's crown into the big tree's: see the report). Round 2: in a file, one after another (abuela, Carmen, Luis, Canelo, the frog, 3 ticks apart): each walks in 4 steps to the same point just inside the opening (PU, screen: a person's or Canelo's feet, the frog's q), then in 4 more through it to just past its line, fading as the old (al 1 - i / 8) and gone; Canelo walks and fades too (moves: animal()), the frog hops twice (one hop to the opening, one through it: the old hop count) and fades. Whoever is under the arch has it drawn over them (front.porton); past its line everyone is faded (al .25 and less), so nobody is seen beyond the left post.
